title: Thrust vs. Steer (or: Yet Another Anecdotal Case of the Dunning-Kruger Effect)
summary: A personal anecdote illustrating the Dunning-Kruger effect in software development, contrasting 'thrust' (pushing forward with confidence despite limited knowledge) versus 'steer' (careful, informed direction). The author reflects on how overconfidence in unfamiliar technical territory led to poor decisions, and how recognizing one's own ignorance improved their approach.
